Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 5:41: And the virtue of confession, they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas, page 231a), is to remove from him all the accusers, and his judgment is handed over only to the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, in these words: and therefore a person must specify his sins, each and every one as it is - for whoever specifies his sins, his judgment is handed over only to the hand of the King, the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, and every [heavenly] court abstains from him - and therefore they must specify the sins of each and every limb, and everything he did specifically. This is what is written, "I acknowledge my sin," and so on, and afterward, "and You forgave the iniquity of my sin, Selah." From where do we learn this? From Moses, as it is written (Exodus 32:31), "please, this people has sinned," and so on; concerning Israel it is written (1 Samuel 12:10), "we have sinned, because we have forsaken the LORD" - and should you say this applies to an individual but not to a community - behold, this verse [about Israel] is written; and should you say this applies to a community but not to their representative [alone] - behold it is written, "and Moses returned to the LORD," and it is written, "and they have made themselves." Why? Whoever specifies his sin, the [heavenly] court abstains from him, because a person brings himself near and is not judged by his own mouth, and moreover he does not leave room for the accuser to teach sin against him - a person's own defect he should mention first, not leaving room for another to speak - then the Holy One, blessed be He, forgives him; this is what is written (Proverbs 28:13), "but he who confesses and forsakes them shall obtain mercy" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 5:42: And along with confession, the abandonment of sin and complete repentance are required, and if not, he is punished, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Bo, page 41a), in these words: and therefore a person must be first to specify his sins - once the accuser sees this, he has no permission to open his mouth against him, and then he is entirely separated from him. If he repents, all is well; and if not, the accuser is found against him and says, so-and-so, who came before us with a bold face, rebelled against his Master, his sins are such and such - therefore it is fitting to be careful in all this, so that he be found a faithful servant before the Holy One, blessed be He - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 5:43: And having spoken, in this chapter, of the things attendant on the fast, let us explain, in a chapter of its own, the things that ease the fast, some in thought, some in deed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:1: The things that ease the fast for the one fasting are these. The first, and the essential one, is performing the commandment of repentance with joy - and he should think that through this affliction he fulfills a commandment of his Creator, and it is fitting to fulfill it with joy, as it is written (Deuteronomy 28:47), "because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy" - and he should think how many mocking people stand at gambling games and other kinds of play day and night and more, not eating nor drinking, and sleep not coming to them - and this is because of the desire of the external husk that the body loves, for this body, from a putrid drop, loves all things from the husk, as is known.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:2: And so, when he considers the love of his Creator, may He be exalted, who was patient with him over his iniquities and did not repay him according to his deeds, and put it into his heart to repent, in order to lighten his punishment from Gehinnom and other kinds of retribution - certainly he will endure, with a pleasant countenance, this small affliction, so as not to come to the great, endless, boundless suffering.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:3: And especially if he is occupied with Torah with desire and love, and considers the particular aspects of love explained in the Gate of Love, without doubt the suffering of the affliction will be eased for him, for Torah is a remedy for all wounds, as they expounded in Eruvin (54a) on "for they shall be an ornament of grace [levyat chen] to your head" (Proverbs 1:9), in these words: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, one who walks on the road without an escort [levayah] should occupy himself with Torah, as it is said, "for a levyat chen." One who has a headache should occupy himself with Torah, as it is said, "they shall be for your head." One who has a sore throat should occupy himself with Torah, as it is said, "and chains for your neck." One who has pain in his innards should occupy himself with Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 3:8), "it shall be healing to your navel." One who has pain in his bones should occupy himself with Torah, as it is said, "and marrow to your bones." One whose whole body hurts should occupy himself with Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 4:22), "and health to all his flesh." Rabbi Yannai's son said: come and see that the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not like the attribute of flesh and blood. The attribute of flesh and blood: a person gives his fellow a medicine, good for one thing and harmful for another; but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so - He gave Torah to Israel, which is a medicine of life for a person's whole body, as it is said, "and health to all his flesh" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:4: And the reason for this is that the Torah is bound to His great Name, YHVH, and this Name is the source of life for all existing things - and therefore, since he is bound to the Tree of Life, he shall not fear evil mishaps, and healing depends on it, as it is written (Exodus 15:26), "any of the diseases that I put upon Egypt I will not put upon you, for I, the LORD, am your healer."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:5: And so Rabbi Abba explained in the Zohar (Parashat Korach, page 176a): he opened, "more desirable than gold, than much fine gold" (Psalms 19:11) - how supernal are the words of Torah, how precious are they, desired above, desired by all - because they are the holy Name, and whoever strives in Torah strives in the holy Name and is saved from everything, saved in this world and saved in the World to Come. Come and see, whoever strives in Torah holds fast to the Tree of Life, and since he holds fast to it, he holds fast to everything, as it is written (Proverbs 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:6: And the reason Torah is called "life" and "marrow for the bones" may possibly be understood from what is explained in the Tikkunim (page 17a), in the discourse of Elijah, who said: within is yud-heh, vav-heh, which is the path of Atzilut - it is the irrigation of the tree in its arms and branches, as it irrigates the tree and it grows through that irrigation. And he further says on: and that spring is like the soul to the body, being life to the body - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:7: And when he occupies himself with Torah in fear and love, and intends the secret of voice and speech, as explained above, which completes the secret of the Name, as explained in the Gate of Holiness - then he is certainly holding fast to the Tree of Life, and shall not fear, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 25b), that Torah without fear and love does not fly upward.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:8: And he should intend, in reading, to unify the Shechinah, as explained in the Gate of Love - and this is "it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it," which is explained in the Tikkunim as said of the Shechinah, and likewise "length of days is in her right hand." And when he reads with this intention, strength is added to him, as it is written (Isaiah 40:31), "but those who wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength," and likewise (ibid. 40:29), "He gives power to the faint, and to those who have no might He increases strength."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:9: And in the Zohar (Parashat Shelach Lecha, page 160b), concerning the inclination's counsel to a person - telling him that one occupied with Torah needs a strong, healthy body, because it saps a person's strength - he refutes this counsel, and says, "but rebel not against the LORD" (Numbers 14:9) - they must not rebel against the Torah, for the Torah requires neither wealth nor vessels of silver and gold. "Neither fear the people of the land" - for [even] a broken body, if he strives in Torah, will find healing in everything - this is what is written (Proverbs 3:8), "it shall be healing to your navel, and marrow to your bones," and it is written (ibid. 4:22), "and health to all his flesh." And all those accusers proclaim and say, make room for so-and-so, servant of the King - therefore, "fear them not, for they are our bread" - they themselves prepare sustenance every day for those who strive in Torah, as it is said (1 Kings 17:4), "and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there," and it is written (ibid. 17:6), "and the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning." "Their defense is removed from them" - what is "defense"? This is the repair of harsh judgment - why is it removed? Because "the LORD is with us; fear them not" - all is removed because of Torah. Happy is the portion of those who strive in Torah for its own sake, for they are literally bound to the Holy One, blessed be He, and they are called brothers and companions - this is what is written (Psalms 122:8), "for the sake of my brothers and companions, I will now say, peace be within you" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:10: Behold, three virtues in the virtue of Torah: the first, that even one who is weak is healed through the Torah; the second, that his livelihood is provided for him; the third, the subduing of the forces of judgment. And the reason for all this is that the Torah is bound to His Name YHVH - and this is "rebel not against the LORD," explained as referring to the Torah, for Torah and His Name are all one, and therefore "the LORD is with us; fear them not."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:11: Further, know that whenever we see one beginning to repent, that if he fasts consecutive days his strength weakens, and it is possible he will fall ill - this is because he is not performing complete repentance, for the essence of repentance is not the fast, but rather the fast is a step toward acquiring humility. And indeed, if in his fast he sins and does not do the things needed for the fast, his fast is not considered valuable before Him, may He be exalted, and then he is not saved from the mishaps of the world, as it is written (Deuteronomy 31:17), "is it not because our God is not among us that these evils have found us" - for the penitent, while fasting, removes himself from being nourished according to nature, as explained concerning "a man of kindness rewards his own soul" in the Gate of Love (chapter 11); and while he is sinning, kindness departs from him, and he remains under nature, and nature does not support him since he is fasting - it follows that he is bald on this side and that, and therefore the fast harms him and he falls ill.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:12: And along these lines the pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz, peace be upon him, explained the mishnah concerning "one who is awake at night" (Avot, chapter 3, mishnah 4), in these words: whoever has a fixed thought in his heart, in his free time deliberates on it - and we are obligated to remember the Torah always, and this is the foundation of the Jew whom He chose from among the peoples. He says (Isaiah 46:8), "remember this, and show yourselves men" - like "and the foundations [ushaya] were laid" (Ezra 4:12) - remember the Torah and make the foundation of Judaism in your hearts. Therefore, whoever, in these free hours, does not remember the Torah, is culpable with his soul. And I have already written, in the mishnah of "one who eats much meat," that everything created in this world is entirely a preparation for Torah, like the parable of salt for meat - and therefore whoever indulges too much in them harms himself, but whoever indulges much in Torah does the opposite, for he holds fast to the Tree of Life, since Torah is the sustaining force of the world. And therefore this wise one said, "one who is awake at night" - which is given for the body's rest - and likewise "one who walks alone on the road" - for from the abundance of the body's motion, the fat of his flesh melts, and therefore he turns his heart to idleness, so as not to add to the weakening of his strength - it is not enough that this does not help him, but he is culpable with his soul - for one who cleaves to his Creator, blessed be He, is watched over by Him and He will not abandon him to mishaps, for He neither slumbers nor sleeps; and even if it saps his strength temporarily, of him it is said (Proverbs 11:24), "there is one who scatters, and yet increases." But if he guards himself in those hours and is anxious to save himself through natural means, then the cleaving between him and his Owner departs from him, and at that time his Creator's providence departs from him - and if any evil befalls him, it is only because he turned his thought away from the service of the Name, as it is said, "is it not because our God is not among us that these evils have found us." And they expounded, of blessed memory (Leviticus 19:4), "do not turn to idols" (Shabbat 149a) - do not turn to your own understanding [i.e., don't rely on your own reasoning against Torah]. And Rabbi Yochanan said, what is desecration of the Name? Such as I, who walk four cubits without Torah and without tefillin (Yoma 86a) - and it is fitting to say so, for every person draws himself near to the place of his life and flees from danger, and since Torah is the tree of life, one who distances himself from it cannot escape one of two things: either he is a fool and does not care about life, or he does not believe in the virtue of the perfect Torah, that it gives life to its possessors - and if so, what desecration of the Name is greater than this? The Tanna spoke only of what is fitting for the soul of one walking on the road or awake at night - and even if he does not consider that we are obligated to the Creator, blessed be He, one who could occupy himself with Torah in restful ease, and is idle, his punishment has no end - and to this King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:97), "O how I love Your Torah! It is my meditation all the day" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:13: And therefore a fasting penitent must be careful in all his ways with complete precision, and be careful of the twenty-four things that hinder repentance, and these are: 1) talebearing, 2) slander, 3) an angry person, 4) one with [improper] thoughts. And these four especially are found in most people, and therefore one must be very, very careful of them - and each and every one of these has, in particular, the power to remove the power of the holy soul and cause an impure power to rest in its place, and then "is it not because our God is not among us that these evils have found us" is fulfilled in him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:14: Further, among the twenty-four things: 5) one who associates with the wicked, 6) one accustomed to a meal that does not suffice its owner [i.e., excessive fasting], 7) one who gazes at forbidden relations, 8) one who shares [in the spoils] with a thief, 9) one who says, "I will sin and then repent" - and included in this iniquity is one who says, "I will sin, and the Day of Atonement will atone" - 10) one who disgraces his teachers, 11) one who causes the many to sin - and included in this iniquity is one who prevents the many from performing a commandment - 12) one who diverts his fellow from the path of a commandment to a matter of transgression, 13) one who uses a poor man's pledge, 14) one who accepts a bribe to pervert justice, 15) one who finds a lost object and does not announce it until he returns it to its owner, 16) one who sees his son going astray and does not protest, 17) one who consumes the plunder of the poor, the needy, orphans, and widows, 18) one who separates himself from the community, 19) one who transgresses the words of the Sages, 20) one who honors himself through his fellow's disgrace, 21) one who suspects the upright, 22) one who hates reproof, 23) one who mocks a commandment, 24) one who curses the community. All these twenty-four things hinder repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:15: And when the penitent is careful not to stumble in these, and not in other transgressions, the power of the supernal soul from the supernal Mother, called "Koach" [power/strength], flows into him. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 113b), that penitents merit a supplementary soul every day, which the rest of the people of Israel merit only on Shabbatot and festivals - in these words: as soon as Israel sinned in the incident of the calf, what is written (Isaiah 50:1)? "And for your transgressions your mother was sent away" - of whom it is said (Proverbs 2:3), "for if you cry after understanding" - she was sent from them and "removed from the earth," and did not descend upon them except on Shabbatot and festivals, and the lower Shechinah remained solitary below and the supernal Shechinah solitary above - and this has already been established, "how does she sit solitary" (Lamentations 1:1) - for previously the supernal Shechinah did not move from them, like the lower Shechinah. Happy are the masters of repentance, for she descends upon them every day, every hour, and every moment - of them it is said (Proverbs 6:22), "when you walk, it shall lead you" - and there is no designated day for them, like for others, upon whom she does not descend except on Shabbatot and festivals; but for the masters of repentance she never departs from them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:16: And the soul is called "man's power [koach]," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayishlach, page 174b) on the verse (Proverbs 24:10), "if you faint in the day of adversity, your strength is small" - in these words: another interpretation, "your strength is small" - come and see, at the time a person is idle from Torah and walks in an unfit path, how many adversaries are ready to become his accusers in the day of distress - and even a person's own souls, which are his strength and might, become his adversary, as it is written, "your strength is small," for it becomes narrow [tzar] toward him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:17: Rabbi Abba said, at the time a person walks in the ways of Torah and all his ways are properly arranged, how many advocates stand up for him, to speak well of him. He opened and said (Job 33:23), "if there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand" - and he further says on: there is a person on the path of truth, and that evil inclination becomes his servant, as it is said, "the vile person is despised... but he serves him" (Proverbs 12:9) - then it ascends and becomes an advocate, and says before the Holy One, blessed be He, this person is meritorious - then the Holy One, blessed be He, says (Job 33:24), "deliver him from going down to the pit," and so on - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:18: We find we learn from this discourse three benefits concerning the matter of repentance. The first, that the soul is called "koach" [power] - besides the plain meaning, that it gives a person power and health, the secret of the matter is that it comes from the place called "Koach," as explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 22, page 68a), "set me as a seal" [kachotam] - "koach" "tam" [power, complete] - "Koach" is the supernal Shechinah, "koach mah" from Chochmah, and of this it is said (Numbers 14:17), "and now, let the power of the Lord be great" - to this point. And so he explained in the Tikkunim (ibid., page 68a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:19: Second, that one who walks the good path has his accuser become his advocate - and so it is also explained in the Zohar (Parashat Toldot, page 144b), on the verse (Proverbs 16:7), "when a man's ways please the LORD, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him" - and he explains there that "his enemies" is the evil inclination, subdued beneath him like a servant, as it is said, "the vile person is despised... but he serves him."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:20: Third, his saying, "at the time a person walks in the ways of Torah and all his ways are arranged" - for it is not entirely dependent on the occupation with Torah alone, but also on deed, namely the performance of the commandments and occupation with acts of kindness - as they said (Avodah Zarah 17b), one occupied with Torah alone is like one who has no God - as we elaborated in the Introduction.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:21: And so he says in the Zohar (Parashat Toldot, page 144b): come and see how much a person must repair his paths before the Holy One, blessed be He, in order to perform the commandments of Torah. And so too there (Parashat Vayetze, page 152b), that when a person holds fast to the ways of Torah, he is loved below, and becomes a beloved of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:22: Therefore, when the penitent is careful and alert in all that has been mentioned, the power of the supernal repentance rests upon him, and "one who comes to purify himself is assisted" is fulfilled in him (Shabbat 104a), and the fast is generally part of purity, as written in the Gate of Love (chapter 11), for one is refined through the fire of the heart, whereby his fat and blood are diminished.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:23: And if a person does not precede his repentance with the aforementioned conditions, the power of repentance will not rest upon him, even though he desires it - as the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (end of the Gate of Repentance): and know, my brother, that repentance comes only from our deeds, not from our words, and the Name shall accompany your soul to reach the will of your Creator, for one who hastens toward that good does not attain it, and the fruit of haste is regret. Awaken, my brother, from the sleep of your foolishness, and have compassion on your soul, which is the most honored of the deposits of the Creator with you. Hasten, my brother, and hasten before your fear comes, for you are not secure in life even for one day, and examine your soul with an examination fitting for one like you, weighed with your intellect - and whoever wishes to reach the will of his Creator should enter through the narrow gate through which the enduring pious ones entered - and we all hope for the good, but it reaches only those who hasten toward it, running to it, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot, chapter 5, mishnah 20), "be bold as a leopard, and light as an eagle," and so on, and David said (Psalms 119:60), "I made haste, and delayed not" - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:24: And so they said in Tanna D'Vei Eliyahu (Zuta, chapter 3), which we copied in the Gate of Fear, from Parashat Ha'azinu, in these words: if a person makes himself righteous to speak truth, an angel is entrusted to him who conducts himself with him in the way of the righteous and speaks truth. If a person makes himself wicked to deceive and lie, an angel is entrusted to him who conducts himself with him in the way of the wicked and deceives and lies. If a person makes himself pious, to endure everything, an angel is entrusted to him who conducts himself with him in the way of the pious and endures everything - as it is said (Jeremiah 17:10), "I, the LORD, search the heart," and so on, and so of David it says (Psalms 18:27), "with the pure You show Yourself pure" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:25: Behold, that at first a person must speak truth and be pious, to endure everything - and then, from heaven, they assist him, and entrust to him an angel who conducts himself with him in the way of the righteous and pious. But the attribute of piety, speaking truth, and other good attributes are not fixed in a person until he gives his soul over to them in such a way that they become almost second nature to him - and this is his saying "a person makes himself," meaning that he accustoms himself to this. And so King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 84:6), "happy is the man whose strength is in You; in whose heart are the highways" - for just as a highway is a straight path on which everyone is accustomed to walk, so a pious person has a highway trodden in his heart to endure everything and subdue the inclination in his heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:26: And the secret of arousal from below is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 77b), in these words: from here we learn that whoever is aroused to purify himself is assisted. Come and see that this is so - for since it is written (Genesis 11:31), "to go to the land of Canaan," immediately, "and the LORD said to Abram, go for yourself [lech lecha]" (ibid. 12:1) - and until he was aroused first, "lech lecha" is not written. Come and see, the supernal matter is not aroused until arousal comes first from below, upon which that supernal matter is released - and the secret of the matter is that the black light does not join with the white light until it [the black light] is aroused first; once it is aroused first, immediately the white light rests upon it - and therefore it is written (Psalms 83:2), "O God, do not be silent; hold not Your peace, and do not be still, O God" - so that the white light never cease from the world; and so (Isaiah 62:6), "those who remind the LORD, take no rest for yourselves" - in order to arouse below, so that the supernal arousal be released - and so, once a person arouses arousal first, then the supernal arousal is aroused - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:27: And so they proved it also in the Zohar, in Parashat Vayigash (end of page 210): "and the spirit of Jacob revived" and afterward "and Israel said" (Genesis 47:27-28) - see there. And so they proved it there (Parashat Terumah, page 135b), concerning "at the appointed time on our feast day" (Psalms 81:4) - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:28: Further, there (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 88a), in these words: Rabbi Yehuda opened, "I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me" (Song of Songs 7:11) - this has already been established, that through arousal from below, arousal from above is found, for there is no arousal above until there is arousal below; and supernal blessings are found only where there is substance, not where it is empty. From where do we learn this? From the wife of Ovadiah, to whom Elisha said (2 Kings 4:2), "tell me, what have you in the house?" - for supernal blessings do not rest on an empty table, nor in an empty place - what is written, and so on? And he proved, at the end of the discourse, the matter from the showbread, that the table always had bread on it. And he further says on: come and see what is written, "I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me" - "I am my beloved's" first, and afterward "and his desire is toward me." "I am my beloved's" - to prepare a place for Him first, and afterward "and his desire is toward me." Another interpretation, "I am my beloved's" - for we have learned that the Shechinah is not found with the wicked; once a person comes to purify himself and draw near to the Holy One, blessed be He, then the Shechinah rests upon him - this is what is written, "I am my beloved's" first, and afterward "and his desire is toward me" - a person comes to purify himself, they purify him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:29: And it is necessary that the penitent be assisted - for when he is blemished in his limbs below, as it were he is blemished above, as it is written in the Tikkunim (page 101a), whoever transgresses a commandment is as though he transgressed against the image of the King - when he purifies himself below, he purifies the supernal limb, which is also blemished and in which blessings do not rest. And so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 87b), in these words: another interpretation, "blotting out your transgressions for My own sake" (Isaiah 43:25) - come and see, the wicked of the world cause a blemish above, for when they sin, mercy and supernal illumination ascend, and the nursing of blessings does not descend below, and this level does not receive the supernal blessings that it nurses below - and therefore, "for My own sake," as explained, so that blessings not be withheld from nursing it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:30: And it has already been explained in the Gate of Fear that the reality of the blemish above is because the soul is emanated from above, and sparks of the supernal holiness are clothed within it, for it lives below only through the power of its supernal roots, which flow vitality into it - if so, when a person purifies his soul, he purifies the sparks of the Shechinah and the other aspects in which the blemish was, for they are many, as explained in the Gate of Fear, and all are purified - and therefore he says "they assist him" in the plural, for they all receive purity with him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:31: And the penitent must consider that all beginnings are hard, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded in the Mechilta, Parashat Yitro, on the verse (Exodus 19:5), "and now, if you will indeed obey My voice" - in these words: "if you will indeed obey" - now, accept this upon yourselves, for all beginnings are hard. "If you will indeed obey" - if a person hears one commandment, they let him hear many commandments, as it is said, "if you will indeed obey"; if he forgets one commandment, and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:32: And the reason is that for all things, the husk precedes the fruit, and the husk must be broken - and so it is explained in the Sabba (Parashat Mishpatim, pages 108a-b), on the verse (Psalms 51:20), "do good in Your favor to Zion," in these words: here is a secret - all the works the Holy One, blessed be He, does, first He precedes with the external thing, and afterward the inward brain; but here it is not so. Come and see, all those works the Holy One, blessed be He, does, and the external thing precedes - the brain precedes in thought, but in deed the external thing [precedes] - for every husk is from the Other Side, and the brain is from the brain [i.e., holy source]; and always the Other Side precedes, grows, becomes great, and harbors hatred; once it has grown, they cast it outside (cf. Job 27:17), "he shall prepare it, but the just shall put it on" - he casts it, that husk, and they bless the righteous of the world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:33: And from this a person may infer for all the commandments - that all beginnings, such as rising early for the synagogue or rising early to study, and likewise concerning the fast, that the inclination shows a person weakness and heaviness of head - and when a person perseveres in the service, he will see that all its arguments are shaky.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:34: And they elaborated in the Zohar, at the beginning of Parashat Vayeshev (page 179b), on this matter, concerning the inclination's arguments, and he says: come and see, for this reason [the evil inclination] precedes with a person on the day he is born, in order to be trusted by him - for when the good inclination comes, a person cannot trust it, and it seems to him like a burden [imposed on him]. Along these lines we have learned: who is the cunning wicked one? This is the one who submits his claims before the judge first, before his fellow, the master of the case, comes - along the lines of (Proverbs 18:17), "he who pleads his case first seems right," and so on. Along these lines is the cunning wicked one, as it says (Genesis 3:1), "and the serpent was cunning" - and he precedes and begins with the person before his fellow, who is the good inclination, comes; he does him harm before it, and he cannot lift his head, as though he were loading upon his shoulder all the burdens of the world, because of that cunning wicked one who came first with him - and concerning this Solomon said (Ecclesiastes 9:16), "and the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard" - because another has preceded him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:35: And he further says on: and therefore people stumble concerning the World to Come; but that righteous one who fears his Master - how much evil he endures in this world, so as not to trust and not participate with that evil inclination - and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves him from all of it; this is what is written (Psalms 34:20), "many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him out of them all." And because of the length of his words, we have skipped some of it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:36: Behold, it is not fitting to believe the arguments of one's inclination - and without doubt the inclination says, do not fast lest you weaken and fall ill, and they will tell you, "bring merit and be excused." And its shattering lies within it - for who caused this? Because he was accustomed to eating and drinking, since the cunning wicked one preceded - so let the good inclination come and accustom itself without eating and pleasure, and endure - and this is "many are the afflictions of the righteous," for the righteous endures suffering and pain in order not to believe his inclination, and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves him from all that suffering. And further, how many healthy and strong people, who indulge in pleasure all their days, suddenly fall ill and die; and how many who fast are healthy and strong - for illness and health are only in His hand, may He be exalted.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 6:37: And from this the penitent should understand not to listen to his inclination - such as concerning immersion, which is contrary to nature, and similarly concerning diminishing his money for charity, and the exertion of his body for the sake of a commandment, and many aspects too numerous to count.
